text:
Marcus (Eng - NYC): hi all — heads up: i'm planning to relocate to Lisbon in June and would like to convert from 1099 contractor to full-time before the move. need clarity on WFH stipend eligibility (i've been receiving monthly contractor allowance), payroll setup, and any Portuguese tax/employer registration implications.
Rina (People Ops): welcome back to the full-time plan! quick q: are you aiming to start as a full-time employee before or after you land in PT? that affects payroll timing.
Marcus (Eng - NYC): want FT start date 2026-06-15 (first day in Lisbon). can we onboard as FT effective that date?
Sam (Payroll): possible but we normally align payroll entity with residency. if you start FT on 2026-06-15 and become PT resident, we'll need to run you on our Portugal payroll for the pay period that includes 2026-06-30.
Marcus (Eng - NYC): got it. what about the contractor WFH allowance — will that transfer? i've been getting $200/month.
Rina (People Ops): policy note: recurring WFH allowance is for employees only. contractor payments stop at conversion. we can add an adjustment in your FT offer (one-time sign-on to bridge) or front-load first month to compensate. which do you prefer?
Marcus (Eng - NYC): prefer a one-time bridging payment to avoid gaps. also will the standing desk i bought as contractor be reimbursed again under FT equipment policy?
Sam (Payroll): we can reimburse one outstanding expense if submitted before conversion. expenses paid while you were a contractor are subject to US tax reporting rules; if we reimburse after conversion on PT payroll, PT tax rules apply. we can gross-up if needed.
Tax (US/PT): high-level tax flags: 1) Portugal requires a NIF (tax number) and social security registration for employees — company must register as an employer in PT to operate payroll. 2) a single employee generally triggers local employer obligations (payroll withholding, social contributions). 3) US-sourced income/tax treaties may apply; you'll likely need to file US return as well. recommend external counsel for cross-border filings.
Marcus (Eng - NYC): oh — so Redwood might need to register in PT as an employer? that seems heavy for one hire.
Tax (US/PT): yes for payroll. it's separate from corporate tax nexus for selling or VAT. Employer registration is routine when you have a resident employee — it's not the same as creating a taxable presence for sales, but we'll confirm with tax counsel.
Rina (People Ops): workflow to move forward: 1) Marcus accepts FT offer (we'll issue an offer with start date 2026-06-15) 2) submit relocation + conversion form: https://hr.redwood.example/relocate-convert 3) attach passport, lease or arrival itinerary, and bank info or NIF once you have it 4) Payroll opens PT employer packet and schedules first PT payroll run.
Marcus (Eng - NYC): done, i accepted the offer in Workday. submitted relocation-convert form just now. PeopleOpsBot: "Case #R-5099 created and assigned to Rina. Reminder: international FT conversion SLA 10 business days."
Sam (Payroll): practicals: please upload your Portuguese NIF when you have it; until then we'll need a local contract and provisional tax classification. also, remove the US contractor invoicing schedule and sign the FT employment contract to stop 1099 payments.
Marcus (Eng - NYC): will i lose 401k/retirement access? how do benefits change?
Rina (People Ops): US 401k doesn't port — Portugal has different retirement system. as FT you'll get Redwood's PT benefits packet (health plan, local pension contributions where applicable). we'll provide a benefits comparison doc.
Marcus (Eng - NYC): shipping household goods — does Redwood cover?
Rina (People Ops): yes, relocation policy covers a shipping allowance up to the threshold; if over, we coordinate with relocation vendor. attach a quote to the case.
Tax (US/PT): last note: if you maintain a US address or bank, double-check where you will be tax resident for the year. that affects the final US tax return and potential social security overlap.
Sam (Payroll): timeline summary: offer accepted 2026-05-05, FT start 2026-06-15. Payroll will run PT onboarding tasks and aim to process first PT pay on the next PT payroll cycle after start.
Marcus (Eng - NYC): appreciated. any paperwork I should prioritize?
Rina (People Ops): upload passport and lease/arrival doc, sign FT contract, and request NIF ASAP after arrival (can be done in person or via tax agent). we'll ping you with checklist.
PeopleOpsBot: "Reminder: please upload relocation quotes and NIF by 2026-06-05 to avoid payroll delays."
Marcus (Eng - NYC): thanks team 60a really smooth so far.
